Kenya’s PFM framework is structured hierarchically: the Constitution is the highest legal authority; Acts of Parliament are primary legislation; and regulations made under Acts are subordinate legislation. Instruments within the same tier are not ranked against one another.

1. Constitution of Kenya, 2010, particularly Chapter 12 — highest authority for public finance.
2. Public Finance Management Act, 2012 — primary PFM legislation.
3. Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015 — primary legislation governing public procurement and asset disposal.
4. Public Audit Act, 2015 — primary legislation governing public audit.
5. County Governments Act, 2012 — primary legislation relevant to county-government financial arrangements.
6. Division of Revenue Acts — annual primary legislation concerning revenue division between national and county governments.
7. County Allocation of Revenue Acts — annual primary legislation concerning allocations among counties.
8. County Governments Additional Allocations Acts — primary legislation concerning additional allocations to counties.
9. Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 — subordinate regulations under the PFM framework.
10. Public Finance Management (Public Investment Management) Regulations, 2022 — subordinate regulations governing public investment management.

The Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Regulations, 2020 are also identified in the official framework, but are omitted to keep the response to ten instruments.
